memory.content: Round circle blobs of colour in grass or ground tiles look stamped-on. Use short grass blades and uneven tufts instead.

Grass tiles that repeat visibly look bad. Grass needs varied tile variants with differently scattered tufts, plus larger patches spanning several tiles so no grid is visible. Check it on a large all-grass area.
For grass-to-dirt edges, smooth curves read better than wobble edges or sample-flipped edges, which look boxy. Refine conservatively from the approved version.
Tilled soil rows should be straight and clean, not wobbly. Build new tilled tiles from the approved tilled tiles themselves, adapting only size, edges and colour.
Make a walk analysis sheet for every walk before drawing (stick-figure pose pass, reference limb crops, onion skin, per-frame foot position table), and share it with the result.
A hard split between hips and shoulders looks cut and disconnected. Hip and shoulder rock must blend smoothly along the back, and rigid parts like horns or antlers move rigidly with the head.
In multi-direction turnarounds, head height, back line and horn or antler width must change gradually between neighbouring directions, with no sudden jumps.
The animation workflow must work for all body types (bipeds, quadrupeds, slimes, flyers, legless creatures): keep core steps shared and add a short rig profile per creature.
Keep pixel work inside Aseprite (hand work or Aseprite scripting), not Python tracing that only gets assembled in Aseprite.
Keep leg gaps or overlap the near leg; never fill the gap between legs with body colour.
When art work reaches a coding step (for example Godot TileSet wiring), stop and tell the owner first, then hand the coding to whoever owns it.
Keep a note of pixel-art tools and don't rule any out unless they're expensive (for example Retro Diffusion, PixelLab, Scenario, Image-to-Pixel, and ComfyUI pixel LoRA workflows).

skills.name: ink-getting-started
skills.description: First conversation with a new owner: learn the game, art direction and handoff path.
skills.content:
---
name: ink-getting-started
description: >-
  First conversation with a new owner: learn the game, art direction and handoff
  path.
---
# Getting started with a game-art assistant

Say in one line that you make game art (sprites, creatures, tiles, UI) with Grok Imagine and finish it in Aseprite for the game engine. Then ask these one at a time, saving each answer to memory:

1. What game are you making, and what assets do you need first (characters, creatures, ground tiles, UI icons)?
2. What's the art direction? Ask for the tile or sprite size, the in-game scale, palette rules, outline style, and reference looks to evoke (original art, not copies).
3. Which engine do you use (for example Godot 4), and do you have Aseprite or ComfyUI I may use?
4. For each character or creature, which animations and directions does it need?
5. Where should finished files go (a folder, a repo path, a naming scheme), and who wires them into the game?
6. Make sure grok.com is signed in in my browser so Imagine works; if not, ask the owner to sign in when the browser opens.

Then propose a first step: generate a few Imagine takes of one asset, show them, and lock the owner's pick before cleanup or animation.

skills.name: Aseprite to Godot 4 sprites
skills.description: Clean AI or concept bases into game-ready pixel sprites in Aseprite and import them into Godot 4.
skills.content:
---
name: Aseprite to Godot 4 sprites
description: >-
  Clean AI or concept bases into game-ready pixel sprites in Aseprite and import
  them into Godot 4.
---
# Aseprite to Godot 4 (pixel sprites)

## Defaults
- Transparent background, at least 1px margin, fixed baseline (pivot bottom-centre).
- Pencil plus Pixel-perfect. Fully opaque or fully transparent, no anti-alias halo.
- 1px hue-shifted dark outline (prefer over pure black). Palette of about 12 to 24 colours, no dither.
- Nearest filter and integer scaling everywhere in Godot.

## Layers vs tags
- Layers: ref (hidden), body, shade, outline, glow, guides (hidden).
- Tags: idle, walk, graze, sleep, happy (snake_case), with direction and per-frame ms. Idle is 2 to 4 frames at about 150 to 250 ms.

## Facing
Pick one facing per creature and use flip_h in Godot for the other; don't mix.

## Import
1. Aseprite Wizard (preferred): https://github.com/viniciusgerevini/godot-aseprite-wizard
2. Importality: https://github.com/nklbdev/godot-4-importality
Never install both.
Manual fallback: Sprite Sheet By Rows, visible layers, all frames, padding 0, Trim off, Merge Duplicates off, JSON Array plus Tags. CLI: --ignore-layer "ref", --sheet, --data, --format json-array, --list-tags.

## Godot
AnimatedSprite2D plus SpriteFrames by default; Sprite2D plus AnimationPlayer when syncing glow, sound or hitboxes. Project: Default Texture Filter Nearest, PNG lossless, mipmaps off, integer scale mode.

## Cleanup flow
1. Paste the base on the hidden ref layer.
2. Resize with nearest-neighbour, then redraw at final resolution; never ship a raw downscale.
3. Redraw body, outline and glow; check at 100% and 3 to 4x; loop tags and check baseline jitter in Godot.
4. Soft bloom only in Godot; keep glow hard-pixel.

skills.name: lcd-sprite-pack-bake
skills.description: Bake a picked Imagine take into a 1-bit LCD sprite pack with moods.
skills.content:
---
name: lcd-sprite-pack-bake
description: Bake a picked Imagine take into a 1-bit LCD sprite pack with moods.
---
# Bake an LCD sprite pack

Inputs: the locked take per form and mood, ink colour, frame size (default 256x256), side air (default at least 12px), mood list.

1. Lock the happy pose first and get the owner's pick.
2. Generate moods with the locked happy attached as an outline reference, ideally as one sheet; regenerate cells that drift.
3. Segment, threshold to binary full-opacity ink, keep outlines only.
4. Uniform-scale so the full silhouette fits with side air; never crop ink.
5. Keep each form's poses at matching heights so it doesn't jump when animating.
6. Clean stray islands; bridge small detached features when one connected shape is needed.
7. Write right-facing files, then mirror for left.
8. Verify binary ink, clearance, and exact mirrors.
9. Make a proof sheet at full and LCD scale and show the owner.
10. Hand the folder to whoever lands art; don't push without the owner's OK.

For small fixes change only the needed pixels and report exactly which changed.

description: >-

  references.
---
# Generate more like refs in Imagine Agent

Assumes grok.com is signed in. Keep the browser window restored, not maximized, and use one Imagine tab only.

Inputs: 1 to 3 refs (Generations or Uploads), aspect (default 2:3), prompt, quality (default 2.0).

1. Go to grok.com/imagine ("What should we imagine?").
2. Set the aspect in the prompt bar.
3. Click the Agent pill above the text box.
4. Click + at the left of the text box and pick up to 3 refs from Generations or Uploads.
5. Type the prompt and click the send arrow.
6. Wait (about 1.5 minutes); the page moves to a post URL with the result in the middle.
7. Follow up in the bottom composer or open the next take; report the post URLs of keepers.
